item.title: Timbaland Sues Ex-Managers For $15 Million After Foreclosure Scare
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Timbaland sought $15 million from former managers, alleging unpaid bills, excess commissions and damage to his business ventures.
item.content:encoded:
Timbaland sought $15 million from former manager Gary Marella and business manager Bruce Seckendorf, accusing them of draining his finances while his mortgage went unpaid.

According to The Hollywood Reporter, he filed the 65-page complaint October 30 in Los Angeles Superior Court. The claims included fraud, civil theft and breach of fiduciary duty.

Timbaland alleged a 2025 foreclosure notice exposed the problems, including unpaid federal taxes and penalties. He accused Marella of taking excess commissions from “Verzuz” payments and his catalog sale, plus mismanaging their Beatclub venture.

THR detailed allegations that Marella took $500,000 extra on each of two $5 million “Verzuz” payments and $775,000 above his stated 10 percent catalog-sale commission.

“The foreclosure was not caused simply because Plaintiffs had no money,” the complaint said, according to THR.

Mono Music Group, LL Business Management and Seckendorf Hasson Reilly & Kobay CPA’s were also named. THR reported that neither man nor their firms immediately responded to its comment requests. The report said both men were fired in 2025.

The catalog sale involved years of Timbaland’s work. Hipgnosis announced the purchase in October 2019, describing a collection of 108 albums and songs. Its announcement included work recorded by Aaliyah, Jay-Z, Missy Elliott and Justin Timberlake. Marella appeared in that announcement as Timbaland’s manager and welcomed the agreement.

Beatclub grew from another idea the two men pursued together. In a 2021 Associated Press interview, Timbaland described calling Marella with his plan for a marketplace that could help lesser-known creators reach established artists.

The proposed model let members set prices and retain their music rights, revenue and publishing royalties. Timbaland also framed the venture as a way to learn the business side of music.

“You’re learning financial literacy,” he told AP at the time.

Marella told AP he backed the idea immediately. Justin Timberlake had joined and said Timbaland was already introducing him to collaborators through Beatclub.

“Verzuz” also had its own history of payment disputes. AllHipHop reported in March 2024 that Timbaland and Swizz Beatz sought unpaid attorney’s fees from Triller following a settlement over the platform. That action concerned Triller’s obligations under their agreement.

item.title: Joe Budden Plays Big Switty In “Law & Order” Murder Plot
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Joe Budden played rapper Big Switty in "Law & Order," where a $300,000 mask deal put his character in a murder investigation.
item.content:encoded:
Joe Budden entered a fictional murder investigation as rapper Big Switty in “Law & Order,” with a $300,000 art deal at the center of his character’s dispute.

His guest appearance came in “Property,” the fourth episode of Season 26, which aired October 29. The episode followed the murder of an antiquities dealer, according to TVmaze’s episode listing.

The cameo followed a real business connection with Wolf Entertainment, the company behind “Law & Order.” Budden had become the host of “Crime in America,” a true crime podcast from Wolf Entertainment, Headline Studio and Budden. Advance Local’s announcement said the first episode debuted August 11, less than three months before his television appearance.

The podcast put him in conversation with local journalists who had been reporting on cases in their own communities. Those interviews drew on Advance Local’s network of reporters across the country. Its stated focus covered both developing crimes and cases those reporters had followed for years. That gave the series room for stories gaining national attention as well as ones that had yet to reach a wider audience.

Headline Studio described an approach built around what had happened, who had been affected and what remained unknown. Its rollout called for new episodes on Tuesdays.

On the scripted show, Switty told detectives that an Egyptian mask he had bought was fake and he wanted his money back, according to Billboard. He said he had been having dinner with his manager and lawyer at 9:30 p.m. the previous night. A threatening voicemail to art broker Andrew Carson brought the character into their investigation.

The show’s way of telling a story had figured in Budden’s music long before this guest spot. In an August 2008 AllHipHop interview, he discussed the song “Who” and his effort to trace changes in Hip-Hop.

Budden said he had wanted to make that kind of record for some time. He explained that he wanted listeners to follow how things began and how the culture changed. He also said he kept the beat simple so it would leave room for what he was saying. The television reference was explicit: “I wanted to do it like a Law & Order episode.”

item.title: MC Lyte Lands Halftime Slot For WNBA Finals’ First Game 7
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: MC Lyte is booked for halftime at the WNBA Finals' first Game 7 as her year of touring and artist-pay advocacy continues.
item.content:encoded:
MC Lyte is headed to the WNBA’s deciding game with a halftime booking at San Francisco’s Chase Center. The San Francisco Chronicle reports she will perform Saturday, October 31, when the Golden State Valkyries host the Atlanta Dream.

Glide Ensemble will sing the national anthem, according to the report.

The WNBA confirmed this is its first Finals Game 7 after Atlanta tied the series 3-3 Thursday. Tipoff is set for 8 p.m. Eastern, or 5 p.m. Pacific.

The booking comes during a year that has put Lyte’s music and her work for other artists in view. She is part of the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame’s 2026 class in its Musical Influence category. Her milestones include becoming the first solo female rapper to earn a Grammy nomination with “Ruffneck.”

On the road, she planned to give fans more than a quick run through her hits. In a September interview with AllHipHop, Lyte described the “Road To The Hall Of Fame” tour as a chance to reconnect with supporters in cities tied to her career.

She planned roughly 90-minute sets that left room for stories and conversation alongside the songs.

“It feels like I’m just returning home,” she told AllHipHop’s Chuck “Jigsaw” Creekmur at the time.

Lyte said she could build those shows around her own catalog without relying on guests. Friends could join her if they were nearby, but she wasn’t counting on cameos to carry the performances.

In that interview, she also discussed acting and directing work and projects involving VanVan, Ariel and DJ Germaine.

Away from the stage, she continued to press for changes in artist pay. SoundExchange honored her in August with its Music Fairness Award, citing her support for the American Music Fairness Act.

The organization said she met with lawmakers again this summer to urge the bill’s passage. That followed a 2024 Capitol Hill visit with DMC and Melle Mel.

She also runs Lyte Up Your Empire to help newer artists learn the music business.

“Advocacy has always been part of my purpose,” Lyte said in the August announcement.

Her tour itinerary also listed Atlanta shows for November 9 and 10, followed by Nashville on November 11.

item.title: Keke Palmer Celebrates KeyTV Emmy Win With A Message For Creators
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Keke Palmer celebrated KeyTV's Daytime Emmy for "Glam Through The Ages" and explained her mission to create chances for others.
item.content:encoded:
Keke Palmer had more than a trophy on her mind after KeyTV’s “Glam Through The Ages” won a Daytime Emmy. Backstage, she brought the conversation back to helping other people get their work made.

The KeyTV Network series took Outstanding Daytime Short Form Program at the 53rd Daytime Emmy Awards on Friday (October 30). The ceremony was held at the Hollywood Palladium in Los Angeles.

Speaking with Extra backstage, Palmer said she founded the network to “produce work that would give other people a platform.” She pointed to the struggle to find opportunities in entertainment as part of the reason for building it.

Palmer said the series used beauty history to explore how her community has been seen and represented over time. The recognition encouraged her because it acknowledged both that subject matter and the network carrying it.

The project had a team behind it. The National Academy of Television Arts & Sciences’ credits list Palmer alongside Lenoria Addison, Sharon Palmer and Max Wyeth as its four executive producers. Patrick Garney was credited as producer, with Justin Coloma directing.

That focus on the people making the work has been part of Palmer’s public explanation of KeyTV for some time. In October 2025, she outlined its mission while discussing “Southern Fried Rice,” the series created by Nakia Stephens. At the time, she was defending the series after viewers questioned its handling of cultural identity. The series placed KoKo Johnson at a fictional Atlanta HBCU. Her character was Korean-American and had grown up with Southern Black parents.

Palmer said then that supporting Black creatives required funding, room to learn through mistakes and chances to put ideas into production more than once. She also stressed paid work for people of color behind the camera. Her goal, she explained, was to help those creators tell stories of their own.

She argued that a viewer’s opinion of a show and the need to support Black storytellers were separate issues.

Palmer also discussed her current mix of projects with Extra, including the podcast “Baby This Is Keke Palmer” and wellness app Practice by Palmer.

“I’m really empowered by this tonight,” she said.

item.title: Gunna Leads N.C. A&T’s 100th Homecoming Concert
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Gunna leads North Carolina A&T's 100th homecoming concert Saturday, with Ella Mai on the bill and Kirk Franklin set for Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Gunna will lead North Carolina A&T’s 100th homecoming concert this Saturday, October 31, with Ella Mai, Yung Miami, KWN and BabyChiefDoit joining the bill.

The Hip-Hop and R&B show starts at 7:30 p.m. at First Horizon Coliseum in Greensboro. The venue currently lists tickets as on sale.

Kirk Franklin follows Sunday, November 1, at Steven Tanger Center for the Performing Arts, according to the university’s announcement. Kierra Sheard Kelly and the university’s Fellowship Gospel Choir join him for shows at 1 p.m. and 6:30 p.m.

The concerts cap a week of homecoming events that began October 25. The school calls the celebration its “Greatest Homecoming on Earth.”

The weekend booking comes during a busy month for Gunna on the music business side. He launched SB THE LABEL with Atlantic Music Group backing in October and took the CEO role. His first roster includes Atlanta artists Casper Bluff, Nechie and Dracc. The launch arrived alongside “pop it,” a single his official website is now promoting. It followed The Last Wun, his 25-track album from August 2025, which featured Offset, Wizkid and Burna Boy.

Ella Mai brings her own new album era to the lineup. She released her third studio album, Do You Still Love Me?, this year, with Mustard serving as executive producer. Her North American tour announcement paired the project with 28 headline dates and support from AMA and Girlfriend.

KWN also has a 2026 project out. The East London singer and producer released and all pride aside in June. Its 11 songs followed with all due respect and her “worst behaviour” remix with Kehlani. The newer project includes “touch myself” and “idea of love.”

For fans heading to the Coliseum, the event page lists prepaid parking and mobile tickets. The building takes cards for parking, tickets and concessions, with mobile payment options accepted at most terminals. Cash is no longer accepted for those purchases.

The Halloween date comes with one practical detail for anyone dressing up: costume masks are on the venue’s prohibited-items list. Small clutch bags can measure up to 4.5 by 6.5 inches. The venue does not provide a bag check or lockers.

item.title: Drake Financed K-Os’s BLackneck With Hundreds Of Thousands
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: k-os received hundreds of thousands of dollars in Drake backing for BLackneck, according to a new Canadian Press report.
item.content:encoded:
Drake put hundreds of thousands of dollars behind k-os’s BLackneck, according to The Canadian Press, giving the Canadian rapper room to make music he said labels were reluctant to fund.

The new report put a financial range on backing k-os had already discussed. In an October 21 interview with Billboard Canada, he described Drake as the album’s financier and executive producer. Drake covered the recording costs while urging k-os to follow his own musical ideas, the rapper explained.

For k-os, that money opened up choices about who could play on the record and how much time he could spend experimenting. The 54-year-old told The Canadian Press at Toronto’s Horseshoe Tavern that established artists face labels reluctant to pay for costly recordings when they already have hits to promote.

“Major labels don’t spend that money on music anymore,” k-os said.

The results included a string section and children’s choir on “Still Number One.” Bob Rock produced “i would never.” Recording locations included his parents’ farm near Whitby, where he also worked inside a camper van from 1984.

The support also came with someone to handle the work of getting sessions together. In the earlier Billboard interview, k-os credited former MuchMusic VJ Matte Babel, DreamCrew’s chief brand officer, with managing the project. He said Babel arranged the studio bookings, stayed in touch and sometimes brought cash to recording sessions.

BLackneck arrived October 30 on Spiritual Tech Records. Apple Music listed seven songs across 22 minutes, with the release following 2015’s Can’t Fly Without Gravity.

The two rappers had made music together long before this album. AllHipHop featured their “Faith” collaboration in August 2010.

K-os told Billboard they reconnected at a club in 2021 or 2022 and exchanged numbers again. Drake asked to hear music, then encouraged him to make a record that reflected his own approach. The backing allowed k-os to bring in the Vancouver String Orchestra. He described the record as drawing on the sounds of the late 1990s and early 2000s, citing influences from OutKast to Shania Twain.

“Our relationship is strictly defined by inspiration,” k-os told Billboard. “We inspire each other.”

item.title: Boosie Badazz Denies Son Ray Ray Robbed Anyone, Says Incident Was A Fight
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Boosie Badazz defended son Ray Ray in a social media video, denying the robbery allegation after his Louisiana arrest.
item.content:encoded:
Boosie Badazz denied that his son Ray Ray robbed anyone, describing the Louisiana incident that led to the teenager’s arrest as a fight.

In a social media video shared by LiveBitez on October 30, the rapper defended his son against the robbery allegation. “Nah, my son ain’t rob nobody, bro. My son ain’t got to do that, bro,” he said.

Boosie pointed to Ray Ray’s Rolex and questioned why his son would steal a cheaper watch. That was his explanation for why he believed the robbery accusation did not fit his son.

The Baton Rouge rapper also described the arrests as an attack on his family. He said the devil had been unable to reach him directly and had instead gotten to him through his children.

Ray Ray, whose legal name is Ivy Ray Hatch, was 18 when deputies arrested him on October 22. The Livingston Parish Sheriff’s Office said a person reported being beaten and robbed in Denham Springs. Deputies had been called to Buffwood Street around 7 P.M. the previous evening.

Authorities booked Hatch on armed robbery, aggravated second-degree battery, possession of a firearm with drugs and possession of drug paraphernalia. A judge set bond at $275,500. Hatch posted it and left the Livingston Parish Detention Center the night of his arrest.

The sheriff’s office had not detailed the property reported stolen or the person’s injuries in the initial local report. Deputies also arrested a juvenile, whose name authorities did not release. That suspect was taken to the Florida Parishes Juvenile Detention Center.

Deputies told WBRZ that Antonio Cooley, 19, and Calei Ely, 18, were also arrested in connection with the robbery case.

Boosie had declined to comment when TMZ initially contacted him about the arrest, as AllHipHop previously reported. His new remarks put his own account of the incident in public.

Months earlier, the family had celebrated Ray Ray’s high school graduation. Boosie shared photographs in May and wrote about his pride in being Ray Ray’s father. He wore his son’s picture on a shirt, while Ray Ray posed in green graduation robes. His sister, Poison Ivi, also congratulated him.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Judge Pauses Nicki Minaj’s $275K Jingle Ball Fight As Her Lawyers Seek Exit
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Nicki Minaj's $275,000 Jingle Ball dispute was paused as a judge set a December hearing on her lawyers' request to withdraw.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj‘s $275,000 Jingle Ball dispute was put on hold as a New York judge set a hearing on her lawyers’ request to leave the case.

Judge Leslie A. Stroth scheduled the hearing for December 1, 2026, at 10 A.M. in Manhattan. AllHipHop obtained the order, signed October 27 and filed October 28.

The firm, Kurzman Eisenberg Corbin & Lever, represents Minaj and Pink Friday Productions LLC. Its request to leave is the issue Judge Stroth set for argument.

The order stated that “all proceedings in this matter are stayed” until the hearing.

Attorney Bruce W. Bieber asked to withdraw on October 23. He cited disputes over how to handle the lawsuit and problems communicating.

Bieber wrote that “the attorney-client relationship has irretrievably broken down such that continued representation is no longer feasible or appropriate.”

The case began in March, when 24/7 Productions (USA) Inc. sued over work tied to the December 2023 iHeartRadio Jingle Ball dates and Minaj’s New York promotion for Pink Friday 2.

24/7 said it advanced more than $255,000 for production expenses and sought $275,149.62, plus interest and court costs. Its complaint brought a contract claim against Pink Friday Productions and an unjust-enrichment claim against Minaj personally.

Hotel costs also became part of the fight. AllHipHop previously reported that 24/7 submitted a Langham New York bill totaling $103,730. It included a $9,500-a-night suite for seven nights and four other rooms. The company said it covered those charges.

Minaj’s defense disputed the debt. In a July 31 filing, her team said the costs had been approved and Pink Friday Productions had already paid the bills. Her lawyers also argued that owning the company did not make Minaj personally responsible for its debts.

Judge Stroth’s new order also laid out how a change of lawyers would work if the firm is allowed to leave.

“ORDERED, that if Kurzman Eisenberg Corbin & Lever, LLP is relieved as counsel, the stay shall continue for thirty (30) days from service of the entered order with notice of entry, or for such other period as the Court directs, to permit Defendants to retain substitute counsel.”

Answering papers are due November 12, with replies due November 23. The December 1 hearing is set for IAS Part 12 at 60 Centre Street.

item.title: Spotify’s Latest AI Play Wades In Wild Waters For Rap
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Spotify is considering a $4 to $5 monthly AI remix add-on, with artist participation being voluntary.
item.content:encoded:
Spotify is getting deep in the AI game.

The streaming beast might soon put a remix studio on your phone, provided you have a Premium subscription and a few extra dollars.

The streaming giant is reportedly targeting the first quarter of 2027 for an AI tool that would let subscribers create covers and alternate versions of existing songs. A reveal could happen around February’s Grammy Awards. The proposed price is another $4 to $5 monthly, although neither the cost nor the launch window is final. Spotify declined to comment to the newspaper. 

Apparently, paying to hear the music was only the beginning. Now comes paying to rearrange it.

The reported possibilities include converting a folk song into a dance record or generating a version that sounds as though another artist performed it. For Hip-Hop fans, that raises some interesting questions about how familiar records could sound with different musical treatments. However, the reporting does not establish that subscribers will have unrestricted access to anybody’s voice or catalog.

Before anybody starts assembling an imaginary supergroup, there is an actual permission process.

Spotify has reached agreements with Universal Music Group, Merlin, Kobalt and Believe. Negotiations with Sony Music Group and Warner Music Group reportedly remain underway. Artists would retain the choice to participate even when their labels have signed agreements.

Spotify’s October 20 announcement with Believe offers a concrete example. Believe and TuneCore artists must first express interest in AI programs, then separately decide whether to join this particular partnership. The companies also confirmed that remix streams would generate royalties for participating artists and rights holders. 

That gives this proposal a different financial structure from somebody uploading an unauthorized remix and collecting attention while the original creators collect frustration.

Spotify says the tool will focus on covers and remixes of existing music. Its Kobalt agreement also provides for participating songwriters to share in the money generated.

My question is whether fans want another monthly bill badly enough to become bedroom remixers. Hip-Hop already knows the creative value of reworking a record. The test here will be whether these AI versions are compelling enough to earn repeat listens.

And for artists, the question is even simpler: How much money actually arrives?

item.title: “Cash Money & No Limit Tour” Sunrise Show Canceled, Refunds Detailed
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: The Cash Money & No Limit Tour's November 6 Sunrise show was canceled. The arena outlined refund steps for ticket holders.
item.content:encoded:
Birdman and Master P’s “Cash Money & No Limit Tour” will not reach Sunrise, Florida, on November 6. Amerant Bank Arena listed the show as canceled and posted refund instructions for fans who bought tickets.

The arena’s notice cited “unforeseen circumstances” without giving a more specific reason. The Friday concert was set for 8 p.m., with Boosie billed as a special guest. No replacement date appears in the notice.

The arena said refunds were available through the original seller and could take up to 30 days. SeatGeek customers do not need to file a request; their refunds will be automatic.

Fans who used resale sites, including StubHub, Vivid Seats or Ticketmaster, should contact those companies’ customer service teams. Anyone who bought tickets at the arena’s box office window should call 954-835-SHOW to provide refund information.

There is still conflicting information online. Promoter BMN Entertainment’s individual Sunrise page continues to display November 6, while its main tour itinerary leaves Sunrise out. The venue’s own page explicitly marks the show canceled.

Before the run, Master P discussed the joint tour and independent business with DJ Greg Street in an August interview for V-103 Atlanta.

The pairing brought artists from both New Orleans labels onto one arena bill. The announced lineup included Juvenile, Mannie Fresh and B.G. alongside No Limit names such as Silkk The Shocker and Mia X. BMN Entertainment promoted the run.

In explaining the collaboration, Birdman and Slim Williams previously described the tour as a celebration of their New Orleans roots and a chance to bring longtime fans together.

The tour began September 11 at Houston’s Toyota Center, then headed to New Orleans the next night. At that hometown stop, B.G. proposed to Brooke Jones onstage at Smoothie King Center. She accepted.

For fans looking at other dates, the promoter’s current schedule still lists Tampa’s Benchmark International Arena on November 7 and Raleigh’s Lenovo Center on November 8, both at 8 p.m.

The remaining listed stops are Chicago’s Wintrust Arena on November 13, Cincinnati’s Heritage Bank Center on November 14 and Cleveland’s Rocket Arena on November 15. Chicago and Cincinnati are set for 8 p.m.; Cleveland is listed for 7 p.m.
